text:
zoe kim: hi all - quick ask. i'll be in vermont helping with childcare over the summer (2026-07-01 to 2026-09-15). can i set a temporary homebase there? curious about WFH stipend adjustments, health plan coverage if my mailing address changes, and any payroll withholding surprises. thanks!

marisa (People Ops): hey Zoe :wave: we can support a temporary satellite homebase for that duration. main things to think about: stipend proration, state payroll withholding (VT has income tax), benefits residency (medical enrollment address), and employer nexus risk if it's extended or you meet other conditions.

zoe kim: ok, VT has income tax — ugh. i don't want the company to end up registering in VT. what's the cutoff that triggers nexus?

tom (Legal): short answer: short, temporary stays usually don't create nexus by themselves, but it depends on whether you perform in-person business activities or set up any company presence. duration matters but so do activities (customer meetings, hiring, signing contracts in-state). for 2.5 months and purely remote/caretaking work, low risk. i'll run a quick check once you file the temp-homebase form.

leo (Payroll): @zoe please include the exact dates and the VT physical address in the payroll email. Vermont state withholding will likely apply for the days you're physically there. we'll prorate state withholding for partial months based on days worked in-state. also let us know if you keep your bank/direct deposit the same.

cecil (Manager): +1 from me. if you need shifted hours to overlap with folks, happy to adjust. also confirm VPN access works from their wifi before you go.

marisa (People Ops): stipend details: the monthly WFH stipend is prorated by calendar days in your declared homebase. July/September will be partial months. equipment shipping: we can ship a monitor/keyboard; if shipping to VT increases cost significantly we'll look at other options (reimbursement).

zoe kim: i might bring my company laptop but would prefer a spare monitor shipped. also does PTO or benefits change if my mailing address switches to VT for 2.5 months?

marisa (People Ops): benefits coverage doesn't change for short moves — your medical plan stays the same. but insurance carrier rules differ by state for in-network providers; check your provider network in VT if you expect to see a doctor. benefits eligibility (401k, FSA/HSA) stays intact. update your mailing address only if you want paystubs mailed there; we recommend keeping primary address as your legal homebase for tax docs unless you're changing residency.

leo (Payroll): note on unemployment/paid leave contributions: state employer rates can vary; payroll will evaluate any employer-side contributions that might change. we'll confirm after we process your form.

tom (Legal): ask: will you be meeting vendors/customers in VT or running any company events? that can change our assessment.

zoe kim: no meetings, no events. purely caregiving and remote work.

hr-bot: policy reminder: Temporary satellite homebase allowed up to 6 months within a 12-month period without formal relocation. See /policies/homebase-remote.md.

marisa (People Ops): next steps: 1) Zoe, submit the Temporary Homebase form (link in pinned messages) with dates & address. 2) Email payroll@redwood.com with dates, physical address, and banking preference; cc leo. 3) i'll route to Legal (Tom) once form is in to confirm low nexus risk. 4) if you want equipment shipped, submit a shipping request and mark it as "temporary location". we'll aim to respond in 48 business hours.

zoe kim: thanks team — i'll submit the form today and ping payroll. really appreciate the quick clarity! :relieved:
